children.label: i
children.prompt: Find the sizes of $\angle B$ and $\angle D$ in terms of $\alpha$.

answer.worked:
$\angle B=180^\circ-\alpha$ because co-interior angles are supplementary when $AD\parallel BC$.

$\angle D=180^\circ-\alpha$ because co-interior angles are supplementary when $AB\parallel DC$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: Hence find the size of $\angle C$ in terms of $\alpha$.

answer.short: $\angle C=\alpha$. Thus opposite angles are equal.
answer.worked:
Using the angle sum of quadrilateral $ABCD$,
$$\begin{align*}\angle C&=360^\circ-\alpha-(180^\circ-\alpha)-(180^\circ-\alpha)\\\angle C&=\alpha.\end{align*}$$
Thus $\angle A=\angle C$ and, from part i, $\angle B=\angle D$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle CDA$ (AAS).

Use two pairs of alternate angles and common side $AC$.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABC$ and $\triangle CDA$:

$\angle BAC=\angle DCA$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel DC$).

$\angle BCA=\angle DAC$ (alternate angles, $BC\parallel AD$).

$AC=CA$ (common side).

Therefore $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle CDA$ (AAS).
Since $\triangle ABC\equiv\triangle CDA$, their matching sides are equal. Hence $AB=DC$ and $AD=BC$.

answer.short:
$\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle CDM$ (AAS).

Use vertically opposite angles, alternate angles and $AB=CD$ from part b.
answer.worked:
In $\triangle ABM$ and $\triangle CDM$:

$\angle AMB=\angle CMD$ (vertically opposite angles).

$\angle ABM=\angle CDM$ (alternate angles, $AB\parallel CD$).

$AB=CD$ (opposite sides of a parallelogram, proved in part b).

Therefore $\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle CDM$ (AAS).

answer.short: $AM=CM$ and $BM=DM$ (matching sides of congruent triangles). Thus the diagonals bisect each other.
answer.worked: Since $\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle CDM$, matching sides give $AM=CM$ and $BM=DM$. Thus $M$ is the midpoint of both diagonals, so the diagonals bisect each other.
